judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives under the same Topic 'Pictograms' (Sub-Theme Data Collection and Presentation). This is a genuine skill dependency, not merely shared hierarchy or wording overlap.

This is a substantive developmental progression within measurement, not mere shared hierarchy or wording overlap, so buildsTowards from the second (non-standard) to the first (standard). Ranks are identical (both PRIMARY THREE), but the source-backed objective sequence within the same length topic supports the direction.

The second SFI (objective 2) has pupils identify differences in arm's length and other body parts used for measurement, i.e. recognizing that non-standard body-based units vary. The first SFI (objective 3) has pupils use metres and centimetres as standard measuring units. Recognizing the variability/inconsistency of body-based measures conceptually motivates and supports adopting standardized units, so proficiency in the second supports success in the first (second_to_first). Same-rank direction is justified by this substantive conceptual progression from non-standard awareness to standard-unit use, not merely by shared topic or numbering.

producer_judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives (same coordinate rank 2). The first (Money topic, Mensuration and Geometry theme) asks pupils to shop with money ≤₦20 using the idea of addition and subtraction; the second (Subtraction topic, Basic Operations theme) asks pupils to mention the need for correct subtraction of numbers and fractions in everyday activities. They sit under different themes/topics, but share substantive conceptual coherence: both connect subtraction to real-world/everyday use, one applying it in shopping and the other articulating its everyday necessity. This is meaningful reinforcement without a clear developmental dependency—an awareness objective and an applied objective at the same grade with no evidence one is prerequisite to the other—so relatesTo (symmetric, null direction) is warranted over buildsTowards. Token overlap ('subtraction', 'pupils should be able to') alone would not suffice, but the shared everyday-subtraction concept does.

judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY TWO Performance Objectives sharing the exact topic '1. Three Dimensional shapes' (Sub-Theme Shapes, Theme Mensuration and Geometry). The first asks pupils to identify the curved surfaces of a cylinder; the second to identify and count the flat faces of a cube and a cuboid. These are complementary 3D-shape surface-identification skills that reinforce one another conceptually, but the evidence shows parallel objectives at the same grade rank (rank 1, gap 0) rather than a justified developmental dependency—identifying flat faces of a cube/cuboid does not clearly enable or precede identifying curved surfaces of a cylinder. Shared ancestry, token/trigram overlap (mostly boilerplate 'pupils should be able to', 'identify', 'the', 'of'), and same-page proximity are consideration signals only, not a build direction. relatesTo best fits the substantive topical coherence without asserting sequence.

Proficiency in coin recognition does not support success in comparing weights, and vice versa.

judgment.rationale: The first objective ('divide a collection of concrete objects into two/four equal parts') sits under Theme NUMBER AND NUMERATION > Sub-Theme Whole Number > Topic Fractions, teaching partitioning into equal parts as a fractions foundation. The second ('change money up to ₦20 into small units and shop...') sits under Theme MENSURATION AND GEOMETRY > Sub-Theme Primary Measures > Topic Money, teaching money exchange and shopping. Both are Primary Two Performance Objectives at the same rank, but they belong to different themes, sub-themes, and topics with no substantive conceptual or skill coherence. The nomination signals are shared-grade ancestry and generic token/trigram overlap ('into', 'and', 'pupils should be able to'), which are non-semantic. Proficiency in equal-part partitioning of objects does not developmentally support making change with money, and vice versa; the surface 'divide/into small units' resemblance is superficial, not a shared curriculum skill.
